newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Second bomb in north Colombia, Medellin toll rises.
newsitem.headline: Second bomb in north Colombia, Medellin toll rises.

text.p: A bomb blast destroyed the Codazzi mayor's offices in a conflict-torn region of northern Colombia early on Thursday -- one day after a deadly explosion in the northwest city of Medellin -- police said.

The attack on the town hall of Codazzi in Cesar province caused no injuries, a police spokesman said. The region has seen increasingly violent confrontations between leftist guerrillas and right-wing paramilitaries. Police said there was no immediate indication of the motive for the attack.

In Medellin, another of the more than 40 people injured in Monday's explosion died in a hospital, bringing the death toll to five, city police chief Gen. Alfredo Salgado said. Five suspects, including two minors, were arrested late on Monday in the hunt for the bombers. Some had firearms and small quantities of dynamite, police said.

Leftist guerrillas were blamed for detonating the 125 pound (70 kg) charge of dynamite in downtown Medellin. Police believe they had targeted the offices of local civic group Asocomunal, whose chairman also headed one of the government-backed civilian self-defence groups known as Convivirs, which rebels and human rights organisations say are little more than legalised paramilitary death squads.
